Record Class PanelPosition

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.trevlar.menukit.api.panel.PanelPosition
public record PanelPosition(PanelPosition.Mode mode, @Nullable InsideRegion screenAnchor, @Nullable OutsideRegion region, @Nullable Supplier<ScreenOrigin> pixelOrigin, int dx, int dy, int priority) extends Record
Where a panel sits: the one placement declaration every host reads (§0065).

Placement is declared once, on the panel. A host (a container screen, a vanilla screen, a slot group, the HUD, a standalone MKScreen) reads this record and resolves it against its own reference: the menu frame, the screen, the slot group's box, the game window, or the screen's own main panel. Adapters no longer take a region; the panel says where it goes, and the adapter only says which screens it appears on.

Modes:

  • PanelPosition.Mode.UNPLACED: no placement declared (the default). A host rejects an unplaced panel loudly, except the standalone-screen builders (MKScreen, CustomContainerMenu), which normalise it: the first unplaced panel becomes main(), each later one region(BOTTOM_CENTER).
  • PanelPosition.Mode.MAIN: a standalone screen's frame: one per screen, centred, the reference its REGION siblings resolve against.
  • PanelPosition.Mode.REGION: outside a reference rectangle via an OutsideRegion (RIGHT_ALIGN_TOP, BOTTOM_CENTER, ...). The rectangle is the host's: the menu frame on a container screen, the slot group's box for a slot-group adapter, the main panel on a standalone screen.
  • PanelPosition.Mode.SCREEN_ANCHOR: on one of the nine InsideRegion spots of the screen (or the game window, for the HUD), inset from the edges it touches.
  • PanelPosition.Mode.CENTER: a screen-centred overlay, drawn on top.
  • PanelPosition.Mode.PIXEL: the outer origin comes from a per-frame supplier, in absolute screen pixels (§0057 Revision): the precision escape.

Two modifiers ride every mode:

  • priority(int): stacking order among siblings sharing a region, and z-order within a host. Lower goes first (closer to the region's anchor edge, and underneath in z). Default DEFAULT_PRIORITY. Ties break by the registering mod's id, then by registration order, so ordering never depends on which mod loaded first. (Replaces RegionAnchor and the enums' priority(int) methods.)
  • offset(int, int): a pixel nudge applied after the panel is placed. It moves only this panel; siblings stack as if it were not nudged. (Replaces the HUD's MKHudAnchor offsets.)

Immutable: priority and offset return a new record.

  • Method Details

    • main

      public static PanelPosition main()
      A standalone screen's main panel, its frame: centred on the screen window; every region sibling anchors to its bounds. One per screen.

    • region

      public static PanelPosition region(OutsideRegion region)
      Outside the host's reference rectangle via region: to the right of the menu frame, below a slot group, above a standalone screen's main panel, and so on. Resolved by RegionMath.resolveMenu(OutsideRegion, Reference, int, int, int, int, int), so it is edge-aware on both axes and auto-scrolls when it would overflow the screen. Siblings sharing a region stack away from the anchor edge in priority order.

    • screenAnchor

      public static PanelPosition screenAnchor(InsideRegion region)
      On a screen-edge spot: a TOP_LEFT back button, a TOP_CENTER title, a HUD panel at BOTTOM_RIGHT. Inset from the edges it touches by the host's inset (the HUD and vanilla screens use RegionConstants.EDGE_INSET, a standalone screen's chrome RegionConstants.SCREEN_EDGE_MARGIN); siblings on one spot stack. Resolved by RegionMath.resolveInside(InsideRegion, int, int, int, int, int, RegionMath.Insets).

    • center

      public static PanelPosition center()
      Centred on the screen as an overlay, drawn on top: the placement for dialogs and popovers. Composes freely with dimsBehind, opaque and tracksAsModal.

    • pixel

      public static PanelPosition pixel(Supplier<ScreenOrigin> origin)
      Pixel-precision placement (§0057 Revision): the panel's outer top-left (the background origin; elements render inside at origin + padding) is exactly what origin supplies, in absolute screen pixels, re-evaluated every frame. Returning null skips the panel that frame: not drawn, claims nothing. No reactive budgets are fed: pixel placement means the consumer owns the exact geometry, on-screen included.
      Parameters:
      origin - per-frame supplier of the panel's outer top-left; null return = skip this frame

    • offset

      public PanelPosition offset(int dx, int dy)
      This position nudged by (dx, dy) pixels after placement (positive x right, positive y down). Replaces any earlier offset. Only this panel moves; siblings in the same region stack as if it had not.

    • priority

      public PanelPosition priority(int priority)
      This position with stacking and z-order priority (lower goes first: nearer the anchor edge, and underneath). Default DEFAULT_PRIORITY.

    • standaloneDefaults

      public static List<PanelPosition> standaloneDefaults(List<PanelPosition> declared)
      The standalone-screen default for unplaced panels, keeping the look of the old BODY column: the first unplaced panel becomes main() (unless one is declared), and each later one region(BOTTOM_CENTER), offset so it sits STANDALONE_STACK_GAP below the one before. Declared positions pass through untouched. Used by MKScreen and CustomContainerMenu, the only hosts that accept an unplaced panel.

      ponytail: the offset assumes every earlier stacked panel is shown; with a middle one hidden, later ones sit 12px lower than the old column did. Upgrade path: a per-region stacking gap on the host, if anyone notices.

      Parameters:
      declared - each panel's declared position, in declaration order
      Returns:
      the position each panel takes, same order
